To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cobalt silicides have been successfully used as an ohmic metal contact for n-type 4HSiC semiconductor.
cobalt silicides have been successfully formed as an ohmic metal contact on n-type SiC, with a low contact resistance and high thermal stability.
the cobalt silicide-based ohmic contact to n-type 4 H-SiC was improved by the use of the two-step anneal process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the improvement of ohmic contacts to the n-type SiC semiconductor using cobalmultilayer structures.
the improvement in ohmic contact performance of the metal contact layer by controlling oxidation during annealing and the reduction of contact resistance.
the development of the ohmic contacts to the 4H–SiC substrate using cobalt silicide, which is a promising material for the application of power electronic devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ohmic contact resistance can be improved by reducing the oxide content in metal contact structures and by the formation of cobalt silicides at the metal/semiconductor interface.
the ohmic contact to n-type 4 H-SiC has been improved by reducing oxide content at the interface of the metal contact layer and SiC substrate.
the ohmic contact resistance of the CoSi2 contact structure on 4H-Sic can be significantly reduced by the two-step thermal annealing process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a low contact resistance and a stable ohmic contact structure can be obtained by using the Co/Si multilayer structure.
the two-step annealed cobalt silicide contact structure can provide a low specific contact resistance, high thermal stability, and smooth interface morphology.
a two-step annealing method is a very effective way to improve the thermal stability and electrical performance of the ohmic contacts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the specific contact resistance is reduced to the level that is comparable to the best results obtained by other methods.
the specific contact resistance of cobalt silicide contact on 4H-Sic has been significantly reduced to the level of 1.8×10-6 Ω cm2.
a two-step annealing technique can be applied for the formation of ohmic contacts on n-type 6H-SiC and 4H-Sic.
